newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mixed, yen and marks fall.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mixed, yen and marks fall.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mixed, with yen and marks weakening as widespread dollar buying emerged and lifted the U.S. currency to the upper end of its trading ranges, traders and analysts said.

The rise in the German deficit both in October and in the first 10 months of 1996, coupled with continued jitters about the European Monetary Union (EMU), kept marks on the defensive all day, they said.
However, the rise in Germany's deficit to 14.5 billion marks in October and to 68.41 billion during January to October became an excuse to buy dollars late in the day.
"The bullish news was put on the backburner after we found no selling from the weak U.S. October housing starts," said Randy Donney, director of capital markets research at Pegasus Econometric Group.

Currency futures remained narrowly mixed, as the dollar stabilized following the release of October housing starts. Starts fell to their lowest level since October 1995, down to a seasonally-adjusted rate of 1.366 million units, versus estimates of 1.443 million units.
Once the U.S. data were released, U.S. traders and dealers began focusing on the increase in Germany's deficit.
The deficit's rise to more than 68 billion marks indicated the country would not meet its EMU deficit target by the end of the year, Donney said.
In addition, the Bundesbank called for a strict Maastricht interpretation and expressed concern about the steep German yield curve.

While the dollar/mark's reaction to the data and news reports was delayed, there was a noticeable reaction in the cash crosses. At the opening, cash mark/yen resumed its decline, testing support at the 74.10 level, while sterling rose to 2.5253, a high last seen in June 1994.
December sterling, which scored a contract high in GLOBEX at $1.6756, set another contract high at $1.6766 in pit trade.
"It's just blatantly obvious to people on the Continent that the mark has to lose strength to join the EMU," Donney said.
"December (marks) must hold the $0.6600 area," one futures trader said. The $0.6600 area is equivalent to 1.5164 spot.
Donney said dollar/marks would have to rise to 1.5095 spot to reverse its recent intraday pattern of lower highs.
The 1.5095 level corresponds to $0.6637 in December marks.
Traders are awaiting the U.S. September trade figures on Wednesday. The U.S. trade deficit is forecast to narrow to $9.5 billion from $10.83 billion in August.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was off $0.000006 at $0.008994, marks were off $0.0018 at $0.6652, Swiss francs were down $0.0021 at $0.7888, sterling was up $0.0048 at $1.6748, Canadian dollars were up $0.0004 at $0.7469 and pesos were up $0.000350 at $0.124500.
